messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sudden p99 tail latency degradation detected for /v1/streaming (hosted). p99=4.2s p95=1.3s error-rate +0.6%  — triggered threshold at 11:07 UTC

ajay: seeing spike on the global dashboard. Pattern: long periods of no chunks, then large burst sends. Starts ~11:06 UTC.

dave: any recent infra churn? deploys? config changes?

lucas: no deploys. Edge proxy queue length jumped and a few upstream sockets showed stalled writes. Looks like write buffers accumulating then flushing.

maria: slicing by product: web chat and mobile sdk sessions most affected. Customer-visible "stutter" in streaming responses. Initial estimate: ~1.8% of active streams impacted.

chris: logs show a cluster of clients with very slow TCP read windows. Proxy keeps connections open and buffers ~50KB before writing, then pushes everything on retry -> long tail.

ajay: mitigation plan: 1) route a portion of streaming traffic to a standby proxy pool with stricter upstream timeouts, 2) lower SSE flush interval at runtime from 200ms -> 30ms, 3) enable temporary per-connection write throttling to avoid big flushes.

dave: ok. Open PD incident and page on-call. I'm taking lead. @lucas take proxy changes, @ajay take runtime flush change, @chris monitor logs and rollback hooks.

ops-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-INC-2055 (severity: P2). On-call: dave.

lucas: applying proxy config to canary (3 pods): `proxy.upstream_idle_timeout=15s`, `proxy.max_buffered_bytes=16384`. Will watch 60s.

ajay: patching runtime: `sse.chunk_flush_ms=30` on canary workers. Staged 10% now. Expect small CPU uptick.

chris: adding a temporary ACL to drop connections that present extremely slow read windows > 60s idle to force reconnection; will be conservative.

lucas: canary looks good: p99 on canary proxies dropped from 4.2s -> 0.95s. Moving 40% of traffic.

maria: updating customer message: "We are investigating intermittent delays affecting a small percentage of streaming sessions. We're routing traffic to healthy proxies and adjusting chunking behavior to reduce stalls. We'll provide updates in 20 minutes." Add note: affected ~1.8%, no message loss.

dave: please include link to status page and support contact.

ajay: rolling SSE flush across rest of runtime fleet in 3 stages (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

incident-bot: PD-INC-2055 status: mitigating.

chris: after 100% roll, global metrics: p99=0.92s, p95=0.88s, error-rate back to normal. CPU increased ~5% on worker VMs but within headroom.

maria: customer impact final estimate: ~1.8% of active streams experienced 2-6s stalls, most recovered automatically within 20s once client reconnected or proxy flushed. No data dropped.

dave: good. Next actions: 1) postmortem (assign to chris), 2) add alert for "chunk-burst" pattern (RN-410), 3) infra hardening for proxy buffer defaults (RN-411), 4) SDK doc update recommending client read-heartbeat (RN-412).

achris: (typo correction) @chris: I'll own the postmortem and timeline.

lucas: note for follow-up: instrument per-connection read-rate and export histograms, and consider adaptive flush strategy based on observed client window.

ajay: also recommend a small change to connection reuse: reduce keepalive window on proxies for streaming endpoints so stale clients don't accumulate.

dave: handoff: @chris you'll be PM for the follow-ups. I'll keep monitoring for the next hour then hand to SRE rotation.

incident-bot: PD-INC-2055 updated: mitigated by proxy routing + SSE flush tuning. Next update scheduled at 3412363920.
